text: Git branching is a key part of modern version control. It lets developers work on different tasks without affecting the main code. A common practice is to create feature branches for new work. Each branch keeps changes separate, so the main branch stays stable. When a feature is ready, developers merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request to review the code and discuss improvements. This workflow helps teams collaborate, catch mistakes early, and keep projects organized. Learning how branches, merges, and pull requests work together makes teamwork smoother and safer.
